Company:
'''Companies''' are [[New World]]'s version of Guilds. A Company is a player-run organization formed to make [[Groups|grouping]] and [[crafting]] easier, as well as to meet friends. Each Company has its own name and flag. Companies often have a way to socialize outside the game itself, such as a Discord server.

Each company is affiliated with one of the three [[Factions]], and players cannot join companies from a faction that does not match their own or before choosing a faction. Factions can be chosen as fast as level 8 as long as the quest to choose a faction is completed. Companies can have up to 100 members.
==Settlements==
{{main|Settlements}}
Large Companies may participate in [[War|Wars]] for territory control, but these groups are often exclusive and require a lot of playtime, experience, and gear to join.  

Settlements are hubs of player activity run by Companies. Settlements are originally established when a [[Territories|Territorial Fort]] is purchased when the Territory is unoccupied. A Settlement can then change hands when a challenging Company wins a War against the controlling Company.

==Hierarchy==
===Governor===
[[File:Permissions - Governor.jpg|thumb]]
The highest rank in a Company. The character that starts a Company will become its Governor. When a Company takes control of a Territory, The Governor of the Company also becomes the Governor of the controlled Territory. They can start Town Projects that result in Settlement upgrades when completed. Setup dues in the form of Territory Upkeep must be paid to the [[Factions|Faction]] your Company is a part of. In order to pay this Upkeep, the Governor can adjust taxes and fees in their Settlement so that travelers and Residents help to pay the Upkeep as they craft, trade, and live in their houses. They also can make their Settlement more desirable to own a home in by focusing on particular upgrades for particular types of players.
===Consul ===
[[File:Permissions - Consul.png|thumb]]
A Governor’s second-in-command. A Company can have as many or as few Consuls as it wishes; Consuls have all of the same permissions and powers as the Governor of the Company and Territory they control save two exceptions:

*Cannot change "Can set the daily Treasury withdrawal limit".

Note that in a new company, the first person invited by the creating Governor will automatically become a Consul.
=== Officer===
[[File:Permissions - Officer.png|thumb]]
Officers have the power to invite members to the company. They can kick other Settler ranked players. They are unable to promote other players as promoting a Settler would give him/her the same rank as the Officer, which is not possible.
===Settler===
[[File:Permissions - Settler.png|thumb]]
This is the lowest rank given to a player in any company in New World. Their permissions are minimalized into chatting with the company and making deposits to the treasury. This should be the default rank for any player you do not trust yet because they just joined the company.

War:
[[File:War board.png|right]]
'''War''' is a 50 vs 50 PVP event that allows [[Company|Companies]] to fight for control of [[Territories]]. Wars are a type of [[Conflicts|Conflict]], and the schedule for them appears in the Conflict[[File:Conflicts.png|35x35px]] tab on your Map. 

Players who want to participate in a war can sign by going to that territory's War Board[[File:Warboard icon.png|35x35px]] in town. It will be next to the town hall. You can also sign up remotely by selecting the territory from your map and scrolling down til you see the sign up button.

Companies initiate war by participating in an Influence Race and Declaring War.
== Influence Race ==
[[File:Influence race.png|right|420x420px]]
'''Influence Races''' are a scheduled open world PVP events with rewards for all participants. Any player who belongs to a [[Factions|Faction]] can participate. There are be 3 Influence Races daily. Each will be in a different territory. They last 45 minutes. 

Factions fight over the territory's Fort and 3 additional Influence Towers/Watches. The ground will glow the color of the controlling Faction. The goal is to kill all players of other factions at the Watch/Fort and hold it in your color as long as possible. To join, simply show up to the territory that has the active Influence Race, flag for PvP, and compete. 
Flagged Players can also complete PVP Missions from the Settlement Faction Representative to earn their team points during the Influence Race. 

If an attacking Faction earns the most Influence before the race ends, they’ll receive bonus rewards, plus the opportunity to declare War. If the defending Faction prevents the attackers from scoring enough Influence within the time limit, they’ll earn bonus rewards for both the Influence Race and the upcoming War. Regardless of who wins, the attacking Faction with the most influence can Declare War. 
== Declaring War ==
[[File:Declare war button appears.png|left|thumb|Declare War button and timer under Race Results]]
For an attacking Company to be able to declare war, they must have at least 25 members and their Faction must first build up enough Influence during an influence race.<ref name=":0">In game tooltip on active Influence Race, 11/8/24.</ref> Companies who have contributed a minimum of 10% towards the state of conflict are able to access the Declare War button.<ref>https://www.icy-veins.com/new-world/war-system-in-new-world#declaring-war</ref><ref>https://youtu.be/cOtmmd_RBzQ?si=pwZrSFUY789bygPK&t=304</ref>  In the unlikely event that no Company contributes over 10%, any Company will be eligible to declare War. 

After the race is over, Companies who participated and are able to Declare War will see a Declare War button on their map for a set amount of time [16 minutes?]. Only a Company's Governor and/or Consul can declare war, so only they will see this button. 

Once you hit the Declare War button, you will be shown the Siege Window showing what time the war will take place. You cannot change this time, only confirm that you want to proceed. This gives Companies who have another War or Invasion at the same time the option to not declare war as it may spread Company personnel and resources thin. 
[[File:War camp.png|thumb|War Bidding]]
Once you confirm the Siege Window, you are taken to a War Bid window. It will ask you to commit the Company's money to paying for defenses by outfitting the War Camp. There are 3 options:

* Tier 1: 6 siege-weapon limit, normal supply rate. Costs 7,500.00 Coin
* Tier 2: 8 siege-weapon limit, high supply rate. Costs 10,000.00 Coin
* Tier 3: 10 siege-weapon limit, highest supply rate. Costs 15,500.00 Coin 

The more your company bids the higher chance you have to be randomly selected to be the Governing company for that specific War. You can select to have the money taken out of the Company Wallet or your Personal Wallet. The Coin spent to declare war will be refunded if your company is not selected. 

==War Roster==
War Rostering is carried out by the Governor or Consul (or those they designate) of the attacking and defending Companies.


The Governor of the Vanguard may select members of that company to participate in 50v50 combat. If there are insufficient numbers in a Company to fill out the ranks of the Vanguard, the Governor may choose from anyone in the Faction, or from volunteers from the third Faction.
==The Battle==
===Overtaking the Fort===
[[File:Defending_the_fort.jpg|thumb|Defending the Fort]]
The battle is won by either successfully capturing or defending the Territory Fort. The attacking Faction must breach the Gates of the Fort to capture the defending Faction's Claim over the Territory. For the Gates to be breached, three Rally Points in front of the Gates must be captured. Once the attacking Faction captures a Rally Point it cannot be re-captured by the defending Faction. Captured Rally Points are designated by the attacking Faction to serve as respawn points or as access to the Armory.
==Weapons of War==
===Attacking===
Members of the attacking Faction are awarded Battle Tokens that can be spent at the War Camp's Armory. These Battle Tokens can be used to acquire Siege Platforms to aid in their attack.
====Siege Platforms====
* [[Cannon Platform]]
* [[Fire Launcher Platform]]
* [[Repeater Platform]]
===Defending===
Defenders can build Siege Weapons along the Fort Walls. The strength of the Siege Weapons is determined by Upgrades earned by completing Town Projects.
====Siege Weapons====
* [[Ballista]]
* [[Explosive Cannon]]
* [[Repeater Turret]]
* [[Fire Dropper]]
* [[Horn of Resilience]]
====Siege Generators====
Siege Generators generate resources for the defending Faction which can be used to repair Gates, Armories, Supply Generators, and Siege Weapons.
===Traps===
Both attacking and defending Factions have access to an arsenal of Traps to be used during Battle.
* [[Inferno Mine]]
* [[Powder Keg]]

Corrupted Invasion:
[[File:Invasion_1.jpg|thumb|The Corrupted descend on a fort.]]
[[File:Corrupted Invasion.png|thumb]]
'''Corrupted Invasion''' is the PvE Fort Defense event in [[New World]].

==Description==
[[The Corrupted]] grow in number and strength as a result of the growth of a [[Territory]]'s [[Settlement]]. When they descend on the Territory Fort in an attempt to overtake the Territory, the resulting event is an Invasion. Players must defend the fort against waves of Corrupted enemies of increasing difficulty. If the players fail to defeat the Corrupted and defend the Fort, the Territory suffers and loses upgrades such as Crafting Stations, Fort Gates, or Fort Turrets. Invasions occur approximately every four days, if [[Corrupted Breaches]] are not closed regularly.<ref>https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/fight-the-world-invasions Fight the World: Invasion</ref>

==Participation==
Players can sign up to participate in an Invasion by placing their name on the Settlement's Town Board. The [[Governor]] of the Territory can hand-pick 10 participants; the remaining 40 slots are selected randomly from those who have signed up. Invasions are limited to only Level 50 players and above.
[[File:Fire Dropper.jpg|thumb]]

==Preparation==
Much like during [[War]], players are awarded 50 Battle Tokens to use at the Armory in exchange for ammunition, potions, and traps. Battle Tokens can also be earned through event participation.

==The Invasion Event==

===Corrupted Enemies===

====Grunts====
Grunts pose little threat but when they swarm, they can quickly take down any target. They focus on destroying structures. If they can't reach one of them, they begin to attack players. After a period of time, they start to frenzy, creating fast, intense, and increased damage while also burning themselves out. We recommended destroying Grunts as quickly possible.

====Raiders====
Raiders are the shock troops of the invading forces. They are skilled, tough and well-equipped. They are more than capable of handling themselves in melee combat. They focus on attacking players but will attack structures if there are no players in range.

====Snipers====
Snipers hang back and take pot shots at players from afar. They prioritize targets on the ramparts and are effective at suppressing turrets. They are also evasive, dodging and ducking to avoid player attacks.

====Bombers====
Bombers are runners with explosives strapped to their back. They run at structures and then blow themselves up, dealing significant damage. It is highly recommended to take them down using ranged weapons because they explode on death.

Bombers deal {{i|Siege}} damage on explosion.

====Brutes====
Brutes are huge, hulking beasts that smash structures. They will occasionally attack players that annoy them but are otherwise focused on destroying defenses. Brutes are very tough and require multiple players in order to defeat.

Most Brute attacks do {{i|Strike}} damage, but they ocasionally do {{i|Siege}} damage as well.

====Bosses====
Bosses can vary. Some are focused on destroying structures while others focus on attacking players. In addition, some of them apply buffs to other invading forces or debuffs to players.

== Rewards ==
Invasion rewards are tied directly to a player’s scoreboard score. <ref>https://www.newworld.com/en-us/game/releases/june-part-2</ref>

Factions:
{{tocright}} Players can join one of the 3 '''Factions''' found throughout the island of Aeternum. Choosing a faction allows for open world PVP. Belonging to a faction also gives the player access to additional missions, gear, and items through '''Faction Representatives''' found in [[Settlements]]. [[File:New World Factions.png|right|400x400px]] === Factions === {| class="fandom-table" |{{Covenant|40px}} |[[Covenant]] |A divine order charged with cleansing the land of heretics and defilers so that its true holy nature and justice can be restored. |- |{{Marauders|40px}} |[[Marauders]] |A ruthless military force hell-bent on establishing a free nation where anyone with the strength to do so can prosper and profit. |- |{{Syndicate|40px}} |[[Syndicate]] |A secretive organization of boundless guile and intellect in search of forbidden knowledge to usher in a new age of enlightenment. |} == How to Join a Faction == Once you wash up on the shores of Aeternum you’re guided through a series of beginner quests. You will need to complete those quests to unlock factions. Once you complete the first few quests, you will be directed to the closest town. Continue to progress through these quests and you will eventually meet the leaders of each Faction. Once you have met each one, you will then be faced with a choice of which faction to join. Each Faction has an Enclave with its own [[Fast-Travel Shrine]] located in [[Everfall]]. These will act as the “quest hub” as you travel through a series of Faction Story Quests to join your faction and progress through its ranks. Faction Story Quests are tracked in the Journal [[menu screens]] under Objectives. You can also use this menu to pin the quest objective to your play screen. == How to Switch Factions == '''You can change your faction once every 60 days. '''To change factions, you simply need to press the default key of “K” and go to the Bio tab. In the bottom left-hand corner, there is a Change Faction button. If you are in a [[Company]] you must first leave the company before you can join a different faction. Upon changing factions, any faction gear that you have purchased from your old faction will be yours to keep. Faction Reputation and [[File:FactionTokens.png|30px|link=Faction Tokens]][[Faction Tokens]] do not transfer to your new faction, but remain as-is in your old faction so they will still be there if you eventually transfer back.
''History note: During the original release of the game, you could switch factions at any time. But some players used this to switch factions often, acting as mercenaries to fight for whichever [[Company]] paid more to have them in [[War|Wars]]. This meant that only the top ~150 people on any server were able to participate in Wars.''[https://www.reddit.com/r/newworldgame/comments/w4ffms/wars_only_being_fought_by_the_top_150_people_on/ Reddit r/newworldgame] ''So the 60-day faction change cooldown was instituted to help prevent this.''

== How Faction Relates to PVP == === Open World PVP === Anyone from any faction can opt-in to [[PvP Combat|PvP]] while in the open world. Once you have joined a faction, you can flag up for PvP in any Sanctuary. Sanctuaries are places where players cannot damage other players. Settlements, Outpost, and Fast-Travel Shrines are considered Sanctuaries. Once in a Sanctuary, you flag by pressing the default key of "U". Once you leave the Sanctuary PVP flagged, you have a 30 second timer until you can damage or be damaged by PVP players from other Factions. When you are ready to unflag, you must return to a Sanctuary and hit the "U" key again to do so. Any players from the same faction can form a group while PVP flagged. You cannot join a PVP group with members of other factions. You cannot join a group of unflagged players while you are PVP flagged. ==Faction Missions== Missions given by your Faction Representative can be used to earn XP, {{Coin}}[[Coin]], and [[File:FactionTokens.png|30px|link=Faction Tokens]][[Faction Tokens]]. You can spend Faction Tokens to unlock Faction-specific styled gear. PVP Faction Missions can also raise or decrease Faction Influence in a territory. *[[Faction Missions]] ==War== * A player can only join companies in their own faction. Factions can go to [[war]] over a territory and fight to control it. This is done by increasing faction influence until the territory goes into Conflict. War can then be declared to occur at a specific date/time selected by the declaring company. If two settlements are controlled by the same faction their settlement storages are linked. Faction Missions:
{{Infoboxitem}}After selecting a Faction, you can accept missions from your Faction representative in any Settlement and complete them in exchange for rewards. Factions offer specialized equipment, act as a source of income, and are the group you work with to wage War on other Territories to expand your Faction’s control of Aeternum.

There is a {{Coin}}[[Coin]] bonus (10x) for your first 3 faction missions done each day.

There are two types of Faction Missions: PvE and PvP. 

=== PvE Missions ===
PvE Missions ask you to do things like defeat creatures, craft supplies, stockpile resources, assassinate high-threat foes, or elite missions which send players to take on Aeternum's most dangerous villains and their minions. Completing a PvE Mission rewards Faction currency, which can be used to purchase Faction-specific equipment and items.

=== PvP Missions ===
PvP Missions ask you to do things like recover tactical information, deliver critical messages or items to another Territory, or patrol an area for opposing Factions. Accepting a PvP Faction mission will auto-flag you for PvP. Unflagging yourself will automatically abandon the mission. Dying during your PvP mission will cause you to fail it and you’ll have to go back and accept another. In addition to rewarding Faction Tokens, completing a PvP Mission also generates Influence for your Faction within that Territory. Generating Influence for the controlling Faction of a Territory Reinforces its control, while generating Influence for a Faction that is not in control Undermines the controlling Faction and brings the Territory closer to being vulnerable to a War Declaration.

* Assassinate - Challenge players to take out specific high-threat foes.
* Elite - Send players to take on Aeternum's most dangerous villains and their minions. These missions are higher difficulty with a higher reward. It's recommended that you bring a friend. <ref>https://www.newworld.com/en-us/june-alpha-update-part-2</ref>
*Control Points - Seize control of a Fort.
*Intercept - Defeat enemy faction members and collect their tears.
*War Camp Loot - Retrieve hidden plans at the enemy’s war camp.

Town Projects:
[[File:Town Project Board.jpg|right|alt=|A Town Project Board.]]
"Town Projects are large scale activities people can work on together to upgrade their Settlement. Town Projects require a significant amount of effort and investment from not only the controlling Company, but also the players that call that Settlement home. Town Projects are activated by a Settlement’s Governor or one of their Consuls. When a Town Project is activated, players in the town can take missions that progress the Project towards completion. These missions award XP and currency (among other things), but more importantly they advance the Town Project. For example, let’s say you want to upgrade your Settlement’s Forge, which will enable Weapon and Armor crafters to create higher-quality arms and armor for their adventures. To do so, you would activate the “Upgrade Forge” Town Project and then you, members of your company, and anyone else living in town can work together to complete the project. Projects include crafting missions."

Town Projects and their status can be found by examining the [[Town Project Board]], present in every [[Settlements|Settlement]], usually near the [[Town Hall]]. The projects are activated by the [[Governor]] or [[Consul]] of the [[Companies|Company]] in control of the settlement. There is a [[Coin]] cost that must be paid to activate a project, that increases with the tier, and varies by project type.

==Types==
===Upgrade Settlement===
Upgrade Settlement projects affect the [[Crafting Stations]] in the settlement. Upgrading these stations will also affect the overall "tier" of the settlement, which will change the name of this project category, and will also be visible on the map, and other places.

*Tier 1 - Hamlet
*Tier 2 - Village
*Tier 3 - Town
*Tier 4 - City
*Tier 5 - Capitol

===Upgrade Fort===
Upgrade Fort projects affect the [[Fort]] in the [[Territories|territory]], where [[War]] and [[Corrupted Invasion|Invasions]] take place. Upgrading the fort will also change its name based on tier.

*Tier 1 - Fort
*Tier 2 - Bastion
*Tier 3 - Keep
*Tier 4 - Castle
*Tier 5 - Citadel

You can upgrade the following elements of the fort:

*[[Gates]]
*[[Emplacement Points]]
*[[Repeaters]]
*[[Burning Oil Vat]]
*[[Warhorns]]
*[[Explosives]]
*[[Ballista]]

===Improve Lifestyle===
Improve Lifestyle projects activate buffs to [[Gathering]], [[Crafting]], or combat in the [[Territories|territory]]. They cost the governing company 15,000 [[coin]] to activate.
====Gathering====

*[[Lumberjack's Spirit]] - Increases [[Logging]] Quantity by 20% for 72 hours.
*[[Farmer's Harvest]] - Increase [[Harvesting|Harvest]] Quantity by 20% for 72 hours.
*[[Miner's Resolve]] - Increase [[Mining]] Quantity by 20% for 72 hours.
*[[Hunter's Bounty]] - Increase [[Skinning]] Quantity by 20% for 72 hours.

====Crafting====

*[[Weaponsmith's Temperament]] - Increase base [[Weaponsmithing]] [[Gear Score]] upon craft for 72 hours.
*[[Engineer's Patience]] - Increase base [[Engineering]] [[Gear Score]] upon craft for 72 hours.
*[[Armorer's Inspiration]] - Increase base [[Armoring]] [[Gear Score]] upon craft for 72 hours.
*[[Chef's Passion]] - Increase the chance of getting additional meals when [[Cooking]] for 72 hours.
*[[Arcanist's Wisdom]] - Increase base [[Arcana]] [[Gear Score]] upon craft for 72 hours.

====Combat==== 

*[[Arcane Blessing]] - Increase [[Corruption|Corrupted]] damage absorption by 20% for 72 hours.
*[[Hale and Hearty]] - Increase base [[Health|HP]] by 10% for 72 hours.
*[[Stalwart]] - Increase [[Defense Recovery]] by 20% for 72 hours.

Housing:
{{tocright}} [[File:Housing_1.jpg|thumb|House variety in a settlement]] '''Housing''' in [[New World]] allows players to own a plot of land and a residence inside a [[Territory]]. Owning a house in a territory makes that player a resident under the guidance of the local [[Governor]] and [[Consul]]s. Decorate houses with [[Furniture|items]] crafted using the [[Furnishing]] skill. [[Trophies]] in houses provide passive bonuses. Expand settlement storage using [[Chests|Storage Chests]]. https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/making-your-mark-on-aternum-settlements-and-governance Making Your Mark on Aeternum - Settlements and Governance ==Territory Standing== [[File:Settlement_4.jpg|thumb|House variety in a settlement]] Players, with at least level 1 [[standing]] in the territory in which they wish to reside, can purchase housing. Standing increases by participating in town projects, crafting items in settlements inside the territory, killing creatures, and taking part in faction missions. Players may, with high enough standing, be able to purchase more than one home in a settlement. Players can have, at maximum, three houses. ==Housing Basics== [[File:House_purchase_menu.jpg|thumb|Purchase menu for a house]] *Along with a one time purchase cost, houses have a weekly [[#Property_Tax|Property Tax]]: **The base value of the property tax is 10% of the base value of the house. For example, a 20k house (even if it was purchased for a lower cost due to the first house bonus or company discounts), will have 2k property tax. **That 10% is further influenced by [[Standing|territory standing]] buffs to lower property tax that you may have selected, and the taxes set by the company that governs the settlement. **If your property tax goes unpaid, you immediately lose access to changing decorations, bonuses, and the ability to host others at your house. **The tax period is 7 days long. *A player may physically acquire the same housing location as one or more other players, but they will only be able to see their own property and decorations unless they are visiting another player's house.https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/making-your-mark-on-aeternum-player-housing Making Your Mark on Aeternum - Player Housing *The version of the house that is displayed to the public is determined by a [[#Decoration Score System|Decoration Score System]]. * House owners can host a party of up to five players at any one time in their home, using a group and a group entry option when entering the house. *Houses can have certain in-game bonuses as: **Recall option every 2 to 4 hours. This is determined by the value of the house and can be refreshed by using a small amount of [[azoth]]. ** Extra [[#Storage Chests|Storage Chests]] can be placed in the house. These storage chests increase the settlement storage and give you access to the storage inside your house. The maximum amount of chests is determined by the value of the house (max. 4). ** Each house enables you to place 5 [[trophies]], which give you a global buff to specific professions, luck, or even combat bonuses. Each trophy type can be applied just once per house. * Limits on some decorations may not be intuitive: ** Certain [[Furniture#Animated|animated decorations]] will count toward a house's pet limit, but those that simply have animated effects may not. ** Some items that give off light do not count toward the light limit while others do. ==Varieties of Housing== [[File:House_menu.jpg|thumb|A House menu]] Houses are spread throughout the Settlements and vary in size and style. Some are overlooking the centre of the town, others are by the Settlement walls; some houses have external space for decoration, and others are nestled tightly between two buildings. Houses can have one to three stories. You may enter a house to preview it before purchase. ===Classification=== There are four tiers of Housing: {| class="fandom-table" ! Tier ! Cost ! Minimum Tax ! Fast Travel Cooldown ! Max # of Storage Chests ! Max # of Decoration Items ! Max # of Pets ! Max # of Lights !Territory Standing Required |- |I | 5,000 |250 | 4 Hours |1 |100 |5 |4 |10 |- |II |10,000 |500 | 3 Hours |2 |125 | 6 |6 |15 |- |III |15,000 |750 |2.5 Hours | 3 |150 |7 |8 |20 |- |IV |20,000 |1000 |2 Hours |4 |200 |8 |10 |30 |} You will get a 5,000 golds discount for your first house purchase. ==Property Tax== Property taxes are collected 7 days after your house purchase, and every 5 days afterwards. Simply put, paying your property tax gives you 3 bonuses for 5 days. (Edit: This has been changed from 5 days to 7 days in Update 1.0.5) # Fast travel to your home. # Global bonuses from the trophies placed in your home. # Ability to decorate your home and receive storage chest bonuses. You will receive a notification and be given the option to pay your tax 24 hours before the due date. Once the payment is made, 5 days will be added onto your time remaining. If you decide not to pay the tax, you will be locked out of fast travelling to your home, you will no longer receive any trophy bonuses from that house, and you will no longer be able to decorate your home. You will still be able to enter your home if you are on site. There are no back taxes, so you are free to pay the tax when you wish to receive its bonuses. At level 55, you may purchase up to 3 houses and each house will have its own property tax that you pay separately. The tax rate is configured at the town hall governor desk and can be adjusted by the governor of the settlement every 24 hours. Unclaimed settlements charge a default property tax rate of 10%. Governors can adjust the tax rate between 5% (low) and 20% (high). Azoth:
==Description==  
[[File:Azoth.jpg|thumb|304x304px]]
'''Azoth''' is a mineral with magical properties that serves as a form of currency. It can be used while [[crafting]] to increase the power of any bonuses that might appear on the crafted item, to respec the [[Weapon Mastery|Mastery Tree]] of a [[Weapons|weapon]], or to [[Fast Travel]] to certain areas you've visited previously.
[[Category:New World]]

Players can enhance their chance of making powerful gear when crafting by adding Azoth to most recipes. The more Azoth that is added, the higher the likelihood of powerful perks, gem slots, or attribute bonuses. Players can also use Azoth to [[Fast Travel|fast travel]] around the world of [[Aeternum]]. The farther a player travels or the more they are carrying at the time, the more Azoth it will require to teleport to their new location.

While Azoth is the primary source of supernatural power on Aeternum, it’s part of a more diverse array of cosmic forces. Indeed, while it’s clearly the cause for resurrection, the presence of Corruption is proof that it’s not the sole source of power.<ref>https://www.mmorpg.com/interviews/interview-talking-azoth-and-magic-in-amazons-new-world-2000122337</ref>

"At its core, it is the life essence of the universe, an immense power capable of producing miraculous effects. Different cultures have given Azoth various names: mana, quintessence, chi, élan vital, prana, and the fifth element. It is believed that Azoth builds and collects in various points in the universe, especially where life is abundant. But its precise origin and purpose are unknown. Earth has always been a rich repository of Azoth, and as a result, has attracted the attention of cosmic powers for millennia. Aeternum serves as a focal point for Azoth, as well as a form of refinery. Large concentrations can easily be extracted, processed, and stored throughout the Eternal Isle. Azoth can be used in a variety of ways. It can enchant items, alter the elements, shape landscapes, instantly transport objects across great distances, and transform or even create living beings. Azoth isn’t sentient nor does it have a will of its own — it’s an unknowable energy that fosters life around it. Pure Azoth glows blue, and if not for the influence of sentient beings, would seed and magnify its surroundings into an idyllic Garden of Eden where nature exists in perfect harmony. The substance requires psyche or will to transform reality in specific ways. For example, the Ancients sensed this energy and tapped into it to create their wonders. Azoth can also be tainted by Corruption, its power used to subjugate, corrupt, and destroy. Mastery and control of this energy source are subsequently at the center of most conflicts on Aeternum." --https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/this-week-in-aeternum-welcome-to-the-eternal-isle

==Fast Travel==
[[File:Fast Travel.jpg|thumb|323x323px]]
Azoth is used as a currency to fast travel around the world of Aeternum. This resource allows players to quickly traverse the map to certain locations as long as they have enough Azoth to do so. In order to fast travel to an area, you must have first visited a [[Settlement]], [[Outpost]], or [[Spirit Shrine]] in that zone; you cannot travel to [[Landmarks]] directly. There are a few factors to consider in fast travel before you depart, the first of which being the cost of Azoth. The cost of Azoth can vary in your journeys. There is always a base cost of 50 Azoth; however, there are additional costs or discounts to consider. The distance between your current location and the location you want to adds a Distance Cost to the total. How much you weight you are carrying adds an Encumbrance Cost. The further you are from your destination the higher the distance cost, as well as the more you weigh the higher the encumbrance cost. By being in a [[Faction]] and/or a [[Company]] you can be eligible for a discount on Azoth cost. Having faction controlled areas also decrease the Azoth cost which can even bring the total down below the base cost of 50 mentioned previously.

Fishing is one of 5 [[gathering]] skills in ''New World''.

==Fishing Hotspots==
{{Main|Fishing Hotspots}}
Fishing Hotspots act like fishing nodes, greatly increasing how fast fish bite your line. See the [[Fishing Hotspots]] page for more details, including a list of what Fishing skill level each hotspot unlocks.

== Bait==
{{Main|Bait}}
Use bait to increase your chance of catching rarer or bigger fish. You can gather, [[Cooking|cook]], and loot different baits.

==Fishing Rods==
{{Main|Fishing Pole}}
A Fishing Pole is the [[Tool]] used in fishing, created with the [[Engineering]] craft. Better poles affect 3 things:

*Increased casting distance
*Tension recovery
*A slight modifier to fish rarity

There are also specific fishing [[Perks]] for rods and [[apparel]].

==Fishing Stories ==
{{Main|Category:Fishing Stories}}
The Fishing Stories (quests) begin with [[Fishing With Shields]], given by [[Michael Shields|Master Fisher Michael Shields]] just west of [[Windsward (settlement)|Windsward Settlement]]. The storyline sends you all over Aeternum, so be ready to enter some dangerous places for your fishing adventures!

==Fish Species and Information==
{{Main|Category:Fish}}
There is a wide array of fish, including several [[:Category:Fish Species|species of fish]], in all the waters (fresh and salt!) of [[Aeternum]]. See the individual fish pages in the [[:Category:Fish|Fish Category]] (under construction) for species, weight/length ranges, where to fish them up, XP gained, what they salvage to, and more!

== How to Fish==
[[File:Fishing Steps.png|right|3339x3339px]]

*Equip a Fishing Pole [[tool]].
**You can get one from the first fishing story, [[Fishing With Shields]], or make one at the [[Workshop]] with [[Fibers]] and [[Green Wood]].
*Find a body of water and stand near it. (You can even fish in some towns!)
*Press '''F3''' to pull out your pole and bait.
**Optional: Press '''R''' to add bait to your line.
*Hold '''LMB''' (left mouse button) to cast your line.
*Release LMB at the desired cast distance.
** A longer cast distance makes fish easier to reel in, as you have more "slack" when they fight.
** When your line lands, the water depth and cast distance will be displayed.
**If your line lands in an active [[Fishing Hotspots|hotspot]], you will see green text that says "Landed on Hotspot!" rather than the depth.
*When you're about to get a bite, it will say '''Get ready!'''
*When you see '''Hook!''' click '''LMB''' to hook the fish. You will have short window of time to do this, shown with the colored circle around the picture of a hook next to a fish, that quickly depletes.
** If you miss the hook, you will have to cast again.
*If hooked, you will get a green checkmark and the message '''Reel in'''. Hold '''LMB''' to reel in.
** You will receive 10 Fishing XP and 5 character XP for hooking the fish.
*Watch the tension meter, and release '''LMB''' to give slack as needed. Do not let the tension raise too high or your line will snap.
**The tension color will go from green, to orange, to blinking red - red means it will snap soon, be careful!
* Reel in the fish until the white circle on the outside of the tension meter completes the circle, and the distance reaches 0.0m.
*Congratulations! You've caught a fish!
**You will receive Fishing XP, character XP, and the fish.
**You can then [[salvage]] the fish to receive items like fish filets, fish oil, and other crafting ingredients.

Gypsum:
[[{{PAGENAME}}]] is a resource that is found by doing a variety of activities. Gypsum can be crafted into [[Gypsum Orb]]s, which can then be turned into special caches called [[Gypsum Cast]]s. Gypsum Casts are gear type specific, and when opened, guarantee an [[Expertise]] bump for that type of gear as well as an item of that type.

==Sources==
*[[Obsidian Gypsum]] - 3 per day: is an 80% drop from any Named Elite level 60+ enemy when they drop a bag, and you need three to craft a Gypsum Orb. You can get unlucky, but in general you should only have to kill 4 Named Elites on average to get your daily allotment. Obsidian Gypsum can generally only drop from open world Named enemies in elite zones. You can find a full list of elligible enemies [https://nwdb.info/db/item/gypsumblack here] under the "dropped by" tab. It also has a 10-13 minute cooldown on dropping, so sitting and farming the same enemy four times in a row won't work. It will take around 40 minutes to get enough Obsidian Gypsum because of the cooldown.
*[[Sapphire Gypsum]] - 2 per day: Defeating the final bosses of The [[Lazarus Instrumentality]] and [[Garden of Genesis]].
*[[Ruby Gypsum]] - 3 per day: Outpost Rush completion
*[[Emerald Gypsum]] - 1 per day: Aptitude leveling reward
*[[Citrine Gypsum]] -  You can obtain Citrine Gypsum by completing the following arenas: Zygoramet's Grove in Edengrove, Eternal Pool Arena in Reekwater, Spire of Melpomene Arena in Reekwater
*[[Amethyst Gypsum]] - Major/minor breach completion
*[[Topaz Gypsum]] - 10 per day: Drops from any level 55+ creatures while under the effect of a daily craftable potion, [[Topaz Gypsum Attunement Potion]]. Do note that your Gypsum Limit counter goes up on drop, not on pickup, so if you miss a bag it's impossible to hit ten.
*[[Diamond Gypsum]] - 3 per day: Rewarded from "special event" activities such as opening presents in the upcoming winter event.

==Details==

You need a full days worth of gypsum to create a single orb.  There is a single exception to this: only 1 Sapphire Gypsum can be used each day. You may be able to stockpile these for future crafts. Gypsum is not collected from the reward containers for breaches, outpost rush, arenas or trade skill aptitude level-ups. You will need to complete the activity in order to receive it as a reward. Each orb will be used to level the Expertise of an item slot and generate an item within the maximum range of that Expertise level. It is approximately 31 Orbs to level a slot from 500 [[Gear Score]] to maximum. When everything is at maximum, they will simply be used to generate items of a chosen slot with a guaranteed GS range of 591-600. 

You will only be able to level up the expertise of each item slot once per day. When you are approaching maximum expertise across all item slots, players will need to do less and less gypsum generating activities per day.

Be sure to also check out this article from our friends at NWDB.info: [https://nwdb.info/guides/gypsum-farming-guide Gypsum Farming Guide]

Attributes:
There are five core '''attributes''' in [[New World]]. Each attribute has different benefits and, at certain thresholds, provides bonuses.

Each player starts with 5 Points in each attribute. Each level grants attribute points, and higher subsequent levels grant more attributes per level; 220 attribute points granted, from leveling, in total. Attribute points can be enhanced with [[Equipment]] bonuses and Item Buffs. Respec is free until level 60. Beyond that level, respecing will cost 50.00 [[Coin]]s. 

For "attributes" not found under the Attributes menu, such as [[Luck]] or [[Aptitude]], see their respective pages.

== Strength (STR) ==
Strength governs your power with melee weapons. Heavy melee weapons, such as [[Great Axes]] and [[War Hammers]], scale their damage exclusively (100%) on Strength, while lighter melee weapons like [[Swords]] and [[Hatchets]] scale their damage primarily (90%) on Strength, but also slightly (65%) on Dexterity. [[Spears]], however, scales primarily (90%) with Dexterity and secondarily with Strength (65%). [[Flails|Flail]] scales primarily on Strength (90%) and secondarily on Focus (65%).

== Dexterity (DEX) ==
Dexterity governs the effectiveness with ranged weapons. [[Bows]] scale off exclusively (100%) with Dexterity, while [[Muskets]], [[Rapiers]] and [[Spears]] have a primary contribution (90%) from this attribute. Lighter melee weapons, such as the [[Hatchet]] and [[Sword]], also see a benefit from Dexterity (65%), but not as much as they gain from Strength (90%).

== Intelligence (INT) ==
Intelligence governs your power with most magical weapons. [[Fire Staff]] and [[Ice Gauntlet]] scales exclusively (100%) with Intelligence, while the [[Void Gauntlet]] scales primarily (90%) with it. [[Muskets]] and [[Rapiers]] scale secondarily (65%) with Intelligence. All the [[damage]] done by weapon-socketed [[elemental]] [[Cut Gemstones|gems]], with the exception of [[Amber]] gems, also scale with Intelligence.

== Focus (FOC) ==
Focus governs your [[healing]] output of healing abilities and the damage of a few weapons and abilities. The [[Life Staff]] scales exclusively (100%) with Focus, while the [[Void Gauntlet]] scales secondarily (65%) with it. [[Flails|Flail]] scales primarily on Strength (90%) and secondarily on Focus (65%). In addition, [[damage]] done by [[Amber]] [[elemental]] [[Cut Gemstones|gems]] socketed in weapons also scale from Focus.

== Constitution (CON) ==
Constitution governs your overall Health pool. The higher your Constitution, the more damage you can sustain before succumbing to your injuries.

== Stations ==

==Amounts Crafted==
As a player's crafting skill increases, the yield for certain crafts increases. This yield can also be increased with the use of [[Skills Gear Farming|skill specific armor]]. For instance, a low level Arcanist might produce one Healing Tincture per crafting attempt, while a high level Arcanist might produce two or more.<ref>https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/crafting-in-new-world Crafting in New World</ref> 

The basis for this increase in yield is calculated by 4 factors:

# The base chance for that tier to create extra items.
# The skill level divided by a factor of 10.
# The refining material used.
# The difference in tier between the refining material used and the final product.

Let's say you mined a lot of [[Iron Ore]], went back to town and wished to smelt some steel for steel tools. In your journeys you found an uncommon material called [[Shelldust Flux]], which is a Tier IV item! You are crafting [[Steel Ingot|Steel Ingots]], which are Tier III. You are refining 75 ingots and your refining skill is 100. Your Extra Material Chance will be 58% for a potential addition of up to 43.5 materials, which round to 43 or 44 materials over time.

The base chance for steel ingots is -2%. We add a 10% chance because 100 Refining Skill divided by 10 is 10. This gives us a Base Extra Material Chance of 8%. Steel Ingots are Tier III, Shelldust Flux is Tier IV. This 1 level positive difference in refining material gives a 50% increased chance for extra material, and we thus have 8% + 50% = 58%!

Mathematically this looks like this:

<math>(Refining Skill/10) + Bonus Item Chance * 100 + Tier Difference Amount * 100.</math>

<math>(100/10) + (-0.02 * 100) + (0.5 * 100) = 58%</math>

There are some items that do not have the base material chance at all, such as keystones for [[expeditions]] or certain legendary (Tier V) items. Many of the Tier V items also have a base chance of -20% and therefore even at 200 refining skill this confers a 0% chance for extra materials.

However, there are gear sets in the game (in batches of 5 for full sets of gear) that give +2% yield each for a total chance of 10% extra while wearing all 5 pieces. This is how some tier V items such as [[Asmodeum Ingot|Asmodeum]] will have a max 10% chance for extra materials!

==Gear Score==
As a player's crafting ability increases, the potential range of gear score for crafted items increases. Eventually, the minimum crafted gear score will also increase. This increase means that gear crafted from a lower-tier material by a highly skilled craftsman could potentially grant a higher gear score than the same item crafted from a higher-tier material by a lesser skilled craftsman.

Mutators:
'''Mutated Expeditions''' (also known at '''Mutations''') are an End-Game progression activity that provides players with exclusive loot. To access Mutated Expedition's player use the Activities menu. '''You must own the New World expansion, Rise of the Angry Earth, to participate in Mutated Expeditions.'''
[[File:Screenshot 2024-08-29 162934.png|thumb]]


Mutated Expeditions are a more challenging and engaging version of existing [[Expeditions]]. These expeditions have been effected by a series of Mutators that augment the enemies found within, increasing the difficulty. Which Expeditions are Mutated and which Mutators they gain varies each week. There are 3 Expeditions that are Mutated each week, with reset time at Tuesday 5:00AM.


There are 3 levels of difficulty for each Mutated Expedition, abbreviated as "M1" (Intermediate), "M2" (Hard), and "M3" (Elite). Before participating in a Mutated Expedition, the character must have first completed the "regular" version of that Expedition at least once. 


At the end of each Mutated Expedition, the group receives a score-based rank: Bronze, Silver, and Gold. Normally, a rank of Silver or Gold is required to access the next M-level in the matchmaking system. Each M-level also has a Recommended Gear Score. You must meet the Recommended [[Gear Score]] to queue via the matchmaking system, but can enter the Mutation directly as group of 3 to 5 players with a lower than recommended Gear Score. Players may attempt up to 35 Mutated Expeditions per week.

==Scoring & Rewards==
Completing Mutated Expeditions rewards items such as rare gear, weapons, and crafting materials. The more difficult the expedition, the better the loot.

'''There are no chests to loot throughout the Mutated Expeditions, they are all found at the end.'''

Score is performance based, taken from a combination of categories. Score is also a shared value for group members.

The following categories count towards the group’s overall score value:
*Time: The better the time, the better the score. Calculated at the end of a run.
*AI Kills: A target value for killing a predetermined amount of enemies within the expedition.
*Takedowns: A target value for killing “Named Enemies” within the expedition.
*Team Wipes: Each team wipe during a boss fight reduces the score by a significant amount.
*Respawns: Each respawn reduces the score by a moderate amount.

There are also Bonus Multipliers for run efficiency, minimal respawning/wiping, speed, and taking down all targets. These are calculated at the end of the Expedition run. The score ranks are Bronze, Silver, and Gold.

Players are also rewarded with [[Dark Matter]] depending on their completion rank.

== Mutation Effects ==
As the difficulty increases the Mutators will also increase. M1 versions will have an Elemental Mutation only, M2 will have Elemental Mutation & Promotion, and M3 will have Elemental Mutation, Promotion, and a Curse.

===Elemental===
Elemental mutations infuse enemies in the Expedition with a specific elemental damage type, increasing their resistance to that damage type, converting a large portion of their damage to that type, and giving them powerful elemental-based abilities.
*[[File:icon_hellfire.png|70px|link=]] Hellfire: Hellfire infuses enemies with fire, allowing them to burn players who oppose them.
*[[File:icon_eternal.png|70px|link=]] Eternal: Eternal infuses enemies with void, granting them them abilities that debuff players or buff their void-infused allies.
*[[File:icon_icebound.png|70px|link=]] Icebound: Icebound infuses enemies with ice, inflicting damage and a slow to those far from them and rooting those that break an ice pillar.

===Promotions===
Promotion mutations grant creatures in the Expedition powerful new abilities.
*[[File:icon_savage.png|70px|link=]] Savage: Savage AI apply healing reduction and cast damaging beams around themselves.
*[[File:icon_indomitable.png|70px|link=]] Indomitable: Indomitable creatures persist through damage with life-stealing abilities and are able to summon a phalanx, blocking all incoming player projectiles.

===Curses===
Curse mutations apply dangerous effects to players, forcing them to work together to overcome the curse’s power. At the highest difficulties, Curses become Empowered, creating additional tactical challenges.

== How Settlements Grow ==
Each settlement starts as a Hamlet and levels up to a Capital by completing [[Town Projects]]. Town Projects provide upgrades to the settlement's Crafting & Refining Stations or to the settlements defensive [[Fort]]. The governing company chooses which Town Project to work on. It is then posted on the Town Project Board outside of the settlement's town hall building. Players can check the town project board to sign up for quests to bring back supplies like wood, iron, and food that will go toward the upgrades.

=== Damage to Settlements ===
Corrupted armies attack settlements during [[Corrupted Invasion|Corrupted Invasions]]. The times of these Invasions are listed in the Map under the Conflicts [[File:Conflicts.png|35x35px]] Tab. Players can sign up to defend a settlement. If they are not successful in fully defending the settlement, Crafting & Refining Stations and Fort improvements may be downgraded.
Territory Upkeep fees also have to be paid every 7 days by the governing company in order to prevent the settlement from downgrading. The company collect fees/tax from players when they use the crafting stations and trading post, which the company then uses to pay the upkeep.

High Watermark System:
'''Important Note:''' As of the October 2023 update, HWM and Expertise are no longer in use. Players with The [[Rise of the Angry Earth]] expansion will be able to receive GS 600-700 items.


'''Important Note:''' As of the December 2021 update, HWM will be replaced by [[Expertise]], though the concept is similar.



Also known as HWM, [[{{PAGENAME}}]] is a system that starts when your character reaches level 60 and governs the power of gear drops you receive in higher level areas.

When an enemy or [[Containers|container]] drops a piece of gear, it rolls on its [[Gear Score]] (GS). As you level, Gear Score normally progresses with character level, so as long as you’re fighting enemies at or above your level, Gear Score should be in a range appropriate for the character.

When a character reaches level 60, this mechanic changes a bit - you gain an upper GS limit (HWM) on drops that gradually increases as more powerful drops appear for you. This upper limit is per-item-type. For [[apparel|armor]], it’s based on the slot type (e.g. head armor, chest armor, ring, etc.) and for [[weapons]] it is based on weapon type (e.g. sword, hammer, musket, etc.)

Only item drops affect your HWM. The moment the item drops, your relevant HWM is increased, regardless of if the item is equipped, or even picked up. Crafting an item or buying one from the [[Trading Post]] does not affect your HWM.

Not all enemies and containers (including Event Reward Containers from [[Outpost Rush]], [[War]], [[Corrupted Invasion]], etc.) are created equal in the case of the HWM system. While there is always a small chance to see a HWM increase when defeating a level 60+ creature or searching a container in a level 60+ [[:Category:Points of Interest|landmark]], each level beyond 60 has a soft upper limit on the likelihood of an HWM increase. Similarly, Event Reward Containers will respect the current HWM and have a small chance of increasing it. HWM increases are reliable up to GS 530 when defeating Level 61 enemies, but chances of seeing something beyond GS 530 from a Level 61 enemy is significantly lower than it is from a Level 62 enemy. Level 64+ enemies are capable of reliably dropping gear up to GS 600.

Each time a level 60+ enemy is defeated and gear isn't dropped that increases its type's HWM, the chance for an increase goes up the next time an enemy is defeated. Additionally, some enemies, such as those found in Elite Landmarks and [[Expeditions]], have a higher base chance of dropping items that increase HWM. Level 60+ [[:Category:Named Enemies|named enemies]] are even more likely to drop HWM-increasing items, and Expedition Bosses will always drop an item that increases your HWM, making them a reliable way to increase HWM.<ref>https://forums.newworld.com/t/dev-blog-high-watermark-system/471125</ref>

PvP Flag:
The PvP flag indicates whether or not you can engage or be engaged in [[PvP Combat]] by a player of an opposing [[Factions]]. If the player's PvP flag is enabled, they are able to be attacked and interacted with by players of the opposite faction. If the player's PvP flag is disabled, they cannot be attacked by a player of an opposing faction, and cannot attack, heal or apply buffs or debuffs to PvP-flagged targets.

Players flagged for PvP receive 50% less durability damage to equipment (both equipped and in their backpack) when killed by another player. Killing a player that has been alive for longer than hour will reward 4x the XP. There are rewards for players that have been alive for longer.

Flagged players also receive a 10% [[Luck]] bonus and a 30% [[Gathering]] Luck bonus. Durability lost from PvP-caused deaths is 10% less than other deaths.

When flagged for PvP, choosing to respawn at a camp activates an incrementally-increasing respawn cooldown: 
* For each subsequent camp respawn, this cooldown increases. 
* If the player chooses to respawn elsewhere (for instance, at a settlement), the cooldown will continue counting down in the background. 
* If the player dies while flagged for PvP while the cooldown is counting down, the time increment will be added to the current value. 
* This makes respawning at a settlement and running back into the fray a great way for players to lower their camp cooldown.

PvP Combat:
There are various types of '''Player vs Player''' '''Combat''' in New World.

== Open World PVP ==
[[File:Open world pvp.png|right|450x450px]]
Anyone from any faction can opt-in to PvP while in the open world. Once you have joined a faction, you can flag up for PvP in any Sanctuary. Sanctuaries are places where players cannot damage other players. Settlements, Outpost, and Fast-Travel Shrines are considered Sanctuaries. Once in a Sanctuary, you flag by pressing the default key of "U". Once you leave the Sanctuary PVP flagged, you have a 30 second timer until you can damage or be damaged by PVP players from other Factions. When you are ready to unflag, you must return to a Sanctuary and hit the "U" key again to do so.


Any players from the same faction can form a group while PVP flagged. You cannot join a PVP group with members of other factions. You cannot join a group of unflagged players while you are PVP flagged.

'''Corrupted Breaches,''' sometimes referred to in-game as "portals", are manifestations of [[The Corrupted]] that spawn in controlled Territories. The size, number, and frequency of Corrupted Breaches increases as the Territory's Settlement increases. Corrupted Breaches are visible on a player's map. The culmination of Corrupted activity within a Territory is the [[Corrupted Invasion]]. Corrupted Breaches spawn every 30 minutes for minor breaches, and 60 minutes for major breaches.
==Territory Corruption Levels==
[[File:Territory Corruption Level.png|thumb|Territory Corruption level as shown from the Map.]]
Corruptions levels for the [[Territories]] can be seen on the map (at certain zoom levels) above the influence bar. The levels range from 1 to 3, 3 being the highest. As the level raises, the amount of breaches in the territory increase, making travel and resource gathering more difficult the longer these Breaches go unaddressed. Closing the breaches in the territory can reduce or slow the level. When the corruption level gets high enough and stays high for a long enough time, [[Corrupted Invasion]] will be scheduled for the territory.
== Closing a Breach==
Corrupted activity turns the terrain dark and red, with low visibility. Corrupted Breaches are guarded by [[The Corrupted]].
Corrupted Breaches must be cleared out by groups of players in order to protect the Territory's Settlement and Fort. The Corrupted will continue to spawn at a Breach until the [[Azoth Staff]] is used to seal the Breach. Clearing a Corrupted Breach offers the possibility of unique rewards.<ref>https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/march-to-battle-corrupted-breaches March to Battle: Corrupted Breachs</ref>

Coin in a players inventory is capped at 1,000,000

Store:
'''Store''' is a game tab where you spend Marks of Fortune in {{New World}}, for cosmetic [[skins]], [[emotes]], [[Companies|company]] crests, [[housing]] items, bundles, and [[consumables]].  All items in the store are available for a limited amount of time and are replaced on a weekly basis. The items available for purchase through the store are often referred to as microtransactions as store items need to be purchased via real-world currencies. <ref>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtransaction</ref>

Marks of Fortune are a currency that allow you buy to items within the store. They will be available for purchase using real-world money. Currently, the conversion rate for real-world currencies to Marks of Fortune is unknown. The currency will be able to be purchased upon release and are provided to you on a weekly basis in the beta.

It is unknown whether new store tabs, items or currencies will be added to the game but the New World developers have announced pay-for-convenience features may be added in the future.<ref>https://dotesports.com/mmo/news/new-world-wont-be-pay-to-win</ref> 
==Store Tabs==
===Featured Deals===
[[File:Store.png|thumb]]
Featured Deals is an area where limited time items that are being promoted will be presented. It is the first tab that is opened when you click on the Store.

===Consumables===
[[File:Consumables.png|thumb]]
Consumables currently consist of dyes that allow you to change the color of your armor. They are purchased in bundles of 5 dyes and are a one time use. Each allotment of 5 dyes is purchasable for 3000 Marks of Fortune.

===Emotes===
[[File:Emotes.png|thumb]]
Emotes are an animation sequence that allows you to portray your feelings or emotions through the actions of your character. These [[emotes]] are different than the default emotes available to you and can only be attained through store purchases. Emotes can be purchased for 4000 Marks of Fortune. 

===Armor Skins===
[[File:Armor Skins.png|thumb]]
Armor skins change the appearance of your [[armor]]. You can change the skin of any type of armor (Light, Medium, Heavy) in the game. These skins can be combined and interchanged infinitely. You can change the appearance of your armor anywhere and anytime. Armor skins can be purchased for 13000 Marks of Fortune.

===Weapon Skins===
[[File:Weapon Skins.png|thumb]]
Weapon skins change the appearance of your [[weapons]]. You can change the skin of your weapon depending on the type of weapon skin purchased (i.e. If you bought a hatchet skin, you can only change the appearance of your [[Hatchets|hatchet]] weapons to that skin). You can change the appearance of your weapons anywhere and anytime. Weapon skins can be purchased for 8500-10000 Marks of Fortune. Depending on the size and type of weapon the amount of Marks of Fortune required to purchase the item will change.

===Housing Items===
[[File:Housing Items.png|thumb]]
Housing items are objects that you can place in your [[Housing|house]] to decorate it. These items are purely decorative and provided no additional benefits to your house. These objects can be used to further personalize your house beyond the items that you can currently [[Crafting|craft]] to [[Furnishing|furnish]] your house. Housing items can be purchased for 12000 Marks of Fortune.

===Company Crests===
[[File:Company Crests.png|thumb]]
Company crests are symbols that you can use to personalize your [[companies]] banner. These banners are portrayed around the territorial forts that your company has purchased. Company crests are bought in packs and include 4 symbols within each pack. Company crest packs can be bought for 4000 Marks of Fortune.

===Bundles===
[[File:Bundles.png|thumb]]
Bundles includes all the previously mentioned available store items that can be purchased. All items that are part are part of a bundle such as Company Crests or Armor Skins will be displayed in this store tab. 

The amount of Marks of Fortune for the items mentioned above may change in the future. All amounts are what has been presented in New World beta.

Territory Governance:
[[{{PAGENAME}}]] and related items are performed through the [[Governor's Desk]] and [[Territory Planning Board]], found in the [[Town Hall]] of each claimable [[Settlements|settlement]].

==Governor's Desk==
The '''Governor's Desk''' is found on the second floor of the [[Town Hall]] of each [[Settlements|settlement]], and is used by the governing [[Company]] to set taxes and other items related to Territory Upkeep.

===Territory Upkeep===
Territory Upkeep needs to be paid every 7 days by the governing [[company]] in order to prevent the territory from downgrading. A territory can also receive downgrades from not successfully defending from [[Corrupted Invasion]]. It can be paid from the player's personal "wallet", or from the company "wallet" ({{Coin}}coin bank).

===Taxes and Fees===
The governing company can adjust rates of taxes and fees once every 24 hours.
====Property Tax====
A weekly tax for residents (players with purchased [[Housing]]) in the territory.
*Range - 5-20%
====Trading Tax====
Taxes on each [[Trading Post]] transaction in the settlement.
*Range - 2.5-25%
====Crafting Fee====
A fee for each item made in the [[Crafting Stations]] in the settlement.
*Range - 0.5-3%
====Refining Fee====
A fee for each resource made in the [[Refining Stations]] in the settlement.
*Range - 0.5-3%

===Payrolls===
The governing company receives income from taxes and fees. Click View Statement to see how much {{Coin}}Coin the company has earned from each tax/fee. It is updated every hour.

==Territory Planning Board==
The Territory Planning Board is used to manage [[Town Projects]] in the settlement.

==Settlement Tiers and Upgrades==
Each settlement starts as a Hamlet and levels up by completing [[Town Projects]]. Settlements begin to level down when upkeep, which is due every 7 days, is not paid by the controlling company or if players fail to repel a [[Corrupted Invasion|corrupted invasion]].
*Hamlet - Tier I
*Village - Tier II
*Town - Tier III
*City - Tier IV
*Capital - Tier V
The territory planning board inside the town hall can be used to manage settlement and fort upgrades and territory lifestyle buffs. Each upgrade or buff triggers a set of town projects on the mission board.
===Station Upgrades===
Stations are: Stonecutting Table, Woodshop, Smelter, Loom, Tannery, Forge, Workshop, Arcane Repository, Kitchen, Outfitting Station.

Crafting stations start at tier 2 and refining stations start at tier 3. There's a minimum of 24 hours between upgrades.

'''Crafting stations'''
*Tier 2 -> 3: 100 gold
* Tier 3 -> 4: 5,000 gold
*Tier 4 -> 5: 10,000 gold
'''Refining stations'''
*Tier 3 -> 4: 100 gold
*Tier 4 -> 5: ? gold

Faction Control Points:
Each region’s fort is a PvP control point that will provide both territory and global rewards for the controlling faction. These faction control points give players a way to engage in open world PvP that directly benefits their faction.

==How To Participate==
Territory forts require players to be PvP flagged to enter them. Forts have a control point which players will battle to claim. If a faction has more players inside the control point than any other faction, that faction will begin to slowly capture the control point. The more players that faction has inside the control point, the faster they will capture it. The status of each fort will be visible on the world map, so everyone can see which factions have claimed forts and which forts are currently being contested. When rival factions are assaulting a control point, region-wide messages will alert players that the location is being contested and draw further attention to the location. Control points will be available to contest immediately upon another company claiming that territory. The only times control points will be inactive will be just before and after Wars and Invasions.

*Control Points will be activated 60 minutes after a War or Invasion is completed. The Control Point is deactivated once a War or Invasion is declared.
*Controlling a fort provides a 5% increase to experience gain and 20% increase to influence within that territory for faction members

==Rewards==

Faction Control Point rewards are about long-term value and controlling specific locations to earn buffs specific to that location. Controlling a fort will grant the faction a set of standard rewards and a fort-specific unique reward.

=== Standard Rewards from any Fort ===
* +5% experience gain within that territory
* +20% influence gain within that territory

'''Equipment''' is the category of item in [[New World]] that contains [[Weapons]], [[Apparel]] and [[Tool|Tools]]. ==Crafted Equipment== Equipment can be crafted by a player using the appropriate [[Crafting]] skill. Crafted equipment will have a [[gear score]] that falls within a range determined by the tier of the item as well as the player's crafting skill ability. If the player chooses to increase the number of [[resources]] spent in crafting, there is a higher chance that the crafted item will have one or more [[Perks]] or [[Empty Gem Socket|Empty Gem Sockets]]. * [[Weaponsmithing|Weaponsmiths]] craft [[Weapons]]. * [[Armoring|Armorers]] craft [[Apparel#Armor|Armor]] and [[Satchels|Bags]]. * [[Engineering|Engineers]] craft [[Bows]], [[Muskets]], [[Blunderbuss]], [[Ammunition]] and [[Tool|Tools]]. * [[Arcana|Arcanists]] craft [[Weapons#Magical Weapons|Magical Weapons]]. * [[Jewelcrafting|Jewelcrafters]] craft [[Apparel#Trinkets|Trinkets]]. It can also be dropped by enemies and found in Boxes. ==Looted Equipment== [[File:Equipment_rarity.jpg|thumb|Examples of equipment rarity]] In addition to crafting equipment, players may obtain equipment by killing and looting creatures. Tougher creatures will drop higher rarity equipment with a higher gear score. The number of perks on a piece of equipment determines its rarity. A piece of equipment can have up to 3 perks.https://www.newworld.com/en-us/news/articles/items-in-new-world Items in New World * No Perks: {{Common}}- This level or rarity does not bind on equip. * 1 Perk: {{Uncommon}} * 2 Perks: {{Rare}} * 3 Perks: {{Epic}} * 3 Perks + Guaranteed Gem Slot: {{Legendary}} Randomly, a piece of non-legendary equipment may have a Gem Slot. ==Named Items== [[File:GlowingLifecrystalStaff.png|thumb|Example of a Named Life Staff]] Named items feature pre-determined perks and gem slots. There is a higher chance of a Named item dropping from more difficult creatures and mutated dungeons, but there are items of this rarity at all skill levels. Unlike regular items, Named items have fixed Gear Scores. ==Trinkets and Bags== *[[Trinkets]] provide passive bonuses. All Trinkets feature a gem slot with a permanent slotted gem. Some perks only appear on Trinkets. *[[Bags]] increase the amount of weight a player can carry and also feature a unique set of perks. ==Equipment Load and Armour Rating == All pieces of equipment have a weight that contributes to the player's equip load. Luck:
{{DisambigMsg|1=Luck mechanism|2=the [[Perk]]|3=Luck (Perk)}} General '''Luck''' is separate from gathering-related luck, and has separate values on a character, but functions similarly. More information is below. ==What is Luck?==
"Luck of the general type (as opposed to the types of Gathering Luck that you see on something like a sickle or a food buff) affects your chances to roll “higher” on our lists of items that come from enemies and containers like stockpiles. In the case of furniture schematics and found furniture items, the higher-end storage items are among the most rare. Increasing your Luck will definitely make this more likely to occur, but as with all luck - there’s no guarantee you’ll get it."Archived Forum https://web.archive.org/web/20211117163000/https://forums.newworld.com/t/dev-blog-update-on-current-issues/504297 "There are two ways we interpret luck: An overall scale that you can think of as a ratio of when things occur or a percentage chance to occur. A relative scale that has a movable odds range based on other values we add into it. Things like [[:Category:Enemies|enemies]] and searchable [[:Category:Containers|containers]] use Method #1 above, where anything in their drop list can occur, and your luck stat increases the likelihood of you getting the less common items in the list. In New World’s loot model, drop tables are divided up into overall rarities, with rarer groupings of items living “higher” on the roll table than more common items. There are entire sets of items that drop less frequently than other sets, and equipment is a great example of how we do this. There are collections of equipment that live at different general probabilities: a “Common” set, “Family” sets, and “Elite” sets. Rarer still are the more context-specific Expedition sets and Named Items. Common items have the broadest possible perk roll variety, Family sets have slightly more narrow perk roll variety and a higher chance to roll perks, and Elite sets only come from Gold-Bar (elite) enemies and have narrower perk rolls and an even higher chance to roll perks. Expeditions items almost always roll some perks, and Named items come with a pre-set selection of perks that don’t roll. Luck doesn’t increase your chance to get higher gear score rolls or roll more perks, but it does increase your chances of seeing item drops that have higher chances of rolling bonuses. [[Gathering|Gatherables]] (but not [[Fishing]]) use method #2 above. As your Luck stat increases, it gradually enables new items to drop from the tables. This means that if your luck values are totally unmodified, there are some items in those tables that it are impossible for you to obtain without a bonus. This is particularly useful for “AND” tables, or tables that give you more things as they roll higher. If we were to use this with “OR” tables, it would actually decrease or even eliminate your chances of getting items in the lower roll ranges of the table (so we don’t do that). We set up these tables to “open up” more as your base luck grows to avoid inundating lower-skill-level players with less-common items that they would have no use for until progressing much further in other, relevant skills. We also use it to plant little surprises and new things to find as you level your gathering skills! Additionally, we don’t use percentages in our data notation, we use integer-based roll ranges to apply probability weights to the chances of a specific thing dropping. For instance, let’s the roll range on regular tree is 100,000 (because it is!), but somewhere above that range, say 105,000, is a chance to get a fish (trees don’t drop fish, this is just an example). When you chop down that tree with unmodified luck, you have a 0% chance to get a fish. But if your luck was modified by say, 10,000, your roll range increases from 0-100,000 to 10,000-110,000, which gives you a (roughly) 5% chance to get that fish when you chop down the tree. If you only increased your luck by 5000, you would have a 0.00001% chance at that fish…but that’s why our luck increases from things like food and equipment are pretty chunky so we avoid cases where your luck value is “stuck” in an unfortunate “ultra low odds of a thing” state. With gatherables in particular, increasing your gathering skill adds base luck to your roll, with Level 200 granting a total bonus of 2000 to your base rolls. There aren’t any cases in the game where not having a luck bonus will prevent you from getting an item as long as the associated Trade Skill is at 200. You can use food and equipment to further increase your drop chances, or even enable some items to drop for you “earlier” in your progression!"Archived Forum https://web.archive.org/web/20230525212645/https://forums.newworld.com/t/dev-blog-update-on-current-issues-2/538731
==How can Luck be increased?== ===General Luck=== There are various methods to increase general luck, sometimes referred to as "loot luck". *The easiest method is to find a Weapon, Armor or Bag with a Luck perk. This value scales based on item Gear Score. *Luck can also be added by using [[Pearls]] in a Gem Socket. The tier of Pearl determines the percentage of luck that is increased. *Consumables like the [[Roasted Monstrous Turkey Dinner]] or [[Defiled Rabbit's Foot]] will also increase the chance at rare items from chests and monsters. *Lastly, trophies placed an a player's house (up to 3) can increase the general luck. See [[Minor Loot Luck Trophy]], [[Basic Loot Luck Trophy]], [[Major Loot Luck Trophy]]. Elite Chest Runs (Guide):
Elite Chest Runs are also known as ECRs or World Tours (WT).

Elite Chest Runs take place nearly round-the-clock in each New World server. 
The general idea is that groups of players will rummage an Elite-Zone or Stronghold in order to efficiently loot Elite Chests.

==Requirements==

* Level 50+
** You can be lower than level 50, but you will be taking a large amount of damage from high-level monsters.
* Elite Chests can ONLY be looted once per 24-hour period, this resets at 5:00am EST.
* If participating in the [[Elysian Wilds]] tour, the player must have the [[New World: Rise of the Angry Earth]] DLC.

== Joining or Hosting==
Often times there are active chest runs on your server, if you pay attention to the "[[File:Channelrecruitmentsm.png|link=]] Recruitment" text chat, you will see people gathering for an Elite Chest Run.

Keep an eye out for chats like "X WT", "X World Tour" or "X ECR".
* If you'd like to join an existing raid-group, type:
** "X WT"
** "X ECR"
** "X TRAIN"
** "X" and then the elite zone you're gathered at.

Hosting an Elite Chest Run is pretty simple, come up with a route you'd like to follow, and invite people from the [[File:Channelrecruitmentsm.png|link=]] Recruitment chat that are looking to participate.

* Common chats follow the lines of:
** "Hosting a World Tour! First stop XXX, Then XXX, Last XXX"
** "World Tour in Progress! Currently at XXX, then XXX -> XXX -> XXX. Type X ECR to join!"

==Loot and Rewards==
The goal from Elite Chest Runs is bind-on-equip items, rare trophy materials, and rare crafting resource. 

* One can hope to find:
** Gear Score 600+ {{Legendary}} Items (Bind on Equip)
** Rare Trophy Materials like [[Loaded Dice]], [[Stacked Deck|Stacked Decks]]
** Rare Crafting Resources like [[Brilliant Animus]] and [[Squirming Vines]] or [[Golden Scarab|Golden Scarabs]]

* Elite Zones also carry gatherable resources:
** Wyrdwood Trees

** Runewood Trees
** Starmetal Veins
** Orichalcum Veins
** Mythril Veins

* If participating in Myrkgard, it also contains 5 Corrupted Portals: 
** Corrupted Portal Caches

Note: The loot is not guaranteed! You will ''get lucky'' in time, but do not expect any items worth selling from every elite chest run loop.
